name: MHRA: sotorasib and liver monitoring
summary: The MHRA's August 2026 Safety Roundup advises more frequent liver function tests for people who recently had immunotherapy before starting sotorasib (Lumykras).
keyPoints: The MHRA's August 2026 Safety Roundup says the sotorasib (Lumykras) product information has been updated.
The MHRA advises more frequent liver function testing for patients who had immunotherapy recently before starting sotorasib.
A review of clinical data found a higher rate of liver injury in this group.
Recent immunotherapy may also be a risk factor for interstitial lung disease.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says that, following an update to the summary of product characteristics for sotorasib (Lumykras), healthcare professionals should carry out more frequent liver function testing in patients who received immunotherapy recently, within the previous three months, before starting sotorasib. The Safety Roundup was published on 25 August 2026.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA cites a review of clinical data that found a higher rate of liver injury (hepatotoxicity) in this group than in patients who started sotorasib more than three months after their last immunotherapy dose or who never had immunotherapy. It adds that recent immunotherapy before sotorasib may also be a risk factor for interstitial lung disease, a group of conditions that cause scarring and inflammation in the lungs.

The MHRA says sotorasib should be withheld in patients with severe liver injury, or if interstitial lung disease is suspected, and points clinicians to the summary of product characteristics for monitoring details. The site's lung cancer page gives background.
